sampling_model.design: One-shot finite-population randomization across \(C\) fixed clusters. Independently across clusters, the known mechanism draws either an exact-count label with probabilities converging to \(r\), or a nominal Bernoulli saturation label with probabilities converging to \(p\).
sampling_model.units: Each cluster contains \(n_0\) units and carries an unrestricted fixed binary potential-outcome vector for every within-cluster assignment; there is no cross-cluster interference.
sampling_model.treatment: Exact-count assignment samples uniformly from \(\mathcal S_k\); nominal label \(\ell\) treats units independently with probability \(m_\ell/n_0\), so target-hit rates equal \(Bp\).
sampling_model.overlap: Exact-count designs lie in \(\Delta_K(\rho)\); every entry of \(B\) is positive for interior target counts.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The table \(f\), hence \(\mu_z\), is fixed external planning information or comes from an external pilot. The calibrated Horvitz--Thompson estimator uses these fixed centers and known hit probabilities; the current trial does not estimate \(\Xi\), and optimization protects against every coupling in \(\Lambda(f,\mu_0)\).
sampling_model.randomness: Potential outcomes are fixed; all probability, expectation, convergence, and regret statements are with respect to the known assignment mechanism only.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Derives sharp bounds on the scalar variance of the difference-in-means estimator from two marginal potential-outcome distributions.
Casts causal partial identification with multiple potential outcomes as a multi-marginal optimal-transport problem and derives exact identified sets.
Characterizes admissible conservative quadratic variance bounds under interference and optimizes the selected bound by a convex program for fixed experimental designs and linear estimators.
Provides randomization-based inference and power analysis for direct and spillover effects under a fixed two-stage design distribution.
Uses variance and power formulas to study saturation design under maintained treatment and spillover structures.
Establishes finite-population central limit theorems for multiple treatment levels, factors, and vector outcomes under assignment-only randomness.
Characterizes multi-arm Gaussian minimax-regret rules for a fixed covariance matrix and gives covariance plug-in asymptotics.
Constructs convergent finite-game approximations for minimax treatment choice after discretizing nature's action space.

body.tldr: One realized assignment per cluster identifies assignment-cell welfare margins but not the cross-policy coupling that determines finite-population covariance. The total calibrated Horvitz--Thompson estimator projects the compatible coupling polytope to the sharp covariance image, and the design minimizes worst compatible pairwise comparison variance. For the worked \(n_0=6\), \(m=(1,2,4)\) menu, the exact-count optimum is \(rStar=(1/3,1/3,1/3)\) with objective \(3/2\), whereas the certified nominal-label optimum has \(BpStar=(250/1383)\mathbf1_3\) and objective \(1383/500\). Thus nominal Bernoulli labels inflate the proved pairwise objective and certified cluster count by \(461/250\). The exact all-selector robust minimax-regret receipt remains open.

project_justification.gap: Two-stage saturation papers either impose covariance structure or use conservative variance formulas. Harshaw, Middleton, and Sävje optimize a single conservative quadratic upper bound for a fixed design and estimator, while sharp variance-bound papers do not choose a saturation randomization and Gaussian minimax-regret papers condition on one covariance matrix.
project_justification.niche: The unoccupied object is a design optimized over the joint covariance set compatible with all assignment-cell margins of one unrestricted fixed schedule.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the sharp finite coupling polytope, proves that no single conservative covariance envelope represents it in every direction, supplies linear-program support certificates, and proves a convex exact-hit allocation theorem with necessary-and-sufficient finite KKT witnesses and an assignment-based regret guarantee. In the six-unit \(m=(1,2,4)\) consumer it gives exact rational designs, objectives, stationarity weights, and the nominal-versus-exact cluster-count factor \(461/250\).

body.related_work: AronowGreenLee2014 is the scalar two-potential-outcome sharp-variance benchmark; the slice-constant two-policy face reduces to its Fréchet--Hoeffding program. GaoGeQian2025 supplies multi-marginal optimal-transport language but neither the saturation-specific covariance projection nor an allocation choice. HarshawMiddletonSavje2026 optimizes one conservative quadratic variance bound for a fixed design and estimator; the present incomparable-covariance result shows why the full directionwise image is different, and the KKT theorem optimizes allocation over that image. LiDing2017 supplies finite-population central-limit machinery. JiangImaiMalani2023 fixes the two-stage assignment distribution, and BairdEtAl2018 studies power under maintained outcome structure. Joo2025 and GuggenbergerHuang2025 inform the still-open all-selector Gaussian receipt. EggerEtAl2022 is the worked Kenya saturation-policy consumer: on the six-unit \(m=(1,2,4)\) menu the proved pairwise-robust receipt gives exact allocations and the nominal-versus-exact objective factor \(461/250\), without claiming an exact all-selector minimax value.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The covariance-set image is sharp conditional on the full assignment-cell marginal table \(f\). A current one-shot trial estimates those margins only asymptotically, and prospective use therefore requires fixed external planning margins or an uncertainty set around them. The theorem does not identify \(\Xi\), does not replace it by zero, and does not claim that \(G(\Sigma(sr,\lambda))=s^{-1/2}G(\Sigma(r,\lambda))\).
body.honest_scope: The proved results cover the total calibrated Horvitz--Thompson covariance image, rational support linear programs, non-representability by one directionwise-sharp covariance envelope, robust pairwise-variance allocation, finite KKT certificates, and the empirical-best regret bound, conditional on fixed planning margins \(f\) and the proposal-specific equal-welfare local boundary. For \(n_0=6\), \(m=(1,2,4)\), the exact pairwise receipt is fully rational: exact-count objective \(3/2\), nominal objective \(1383/500\), and cluster-count ratio \(461/250\). The odd \(15\)-cell slices force \(\Xi_{kk}\ge1/900\). The exact robust all-Borel-selector design and a terminating all-minimizer receipt remain open; no total numerical equality oracle is claimed.
